articles.title: Accumulation of FAM98B and tRNA-Splicing Ligase Complex Proteins in Neuronal Intranuclear Inclusions in Spinocerebellar ataxia type 4.
articles.content: Background and Objectives: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 4 (SCA4) is caused by a GGC-repeat expansion in ZFHX3 encoding an expanded polyglycine tract causing p62- and ubiquitin-positive neuronal intranuclear inclusions (NIIs). In multiple polyglycine diseases NIIs sequester tRNA-splicing ligase complex (tRNA-LC) proteins, causing downstream functional defects linked to neurodegeneration. We assessed the localization of tRNA-LC proteins in SCA4 pontine neurons. Methods: Postmortem brain tissue from a genetically confirmed SCA4 patient was examined across multiple regions using immunofluorescence confocal microscopy for p62, ubiquitin and tRNA-LC proteins FAM98B, RTRAF, and RTCB. Results: In pontine neurons, FAM98B, RTRAF, and RTCB were incorporated into NII, accumulating in a distinct outer layer respective to a ubiquitin inner layer. This redistribution was accompanied by depletion of all three proteins from the soluble nucleoplasm. Discussion: Our findings link SCA4 to a tRNA-LC dysfunction phenotype shared by multiple GGC-repeat disorders, further supporting a unified pathological mechanism in polyglycine diseases.
articles.author: Gandelman, M., Figueroa, K. P., Classen, A., Scoles, D. R., Pulst, S. M.

articles.title: Coordinated orienting behavior emerges following unilateral optogenetic activation of Superior Colliculus GABAergic neurons
articles.content: Orienting coordinates movements of the eyes, whiskers, nose, and other effectors, but how the superior colliculus (SC) recruits these components over time remains unclear. We combined unilateral optogenetic activation of SC GABAergic neurons with high-speed tracking of facial movements and Neuropixels recordings to examine SC-evoked orienting in head-fixed mice. Stimulation recruited movements of the whiskers, nose, eyes, and pupil. Horizontal eye and nose movements were directed contralateral to the stimulated hemisphere, whereas vertical eye movements, pupil dilation, and whisker protraction did not differ significantly between stimulation sides. Nose and whisker movements generally preceded eye movements, followed by slower pupil dilation, revealing a temporally organized response. Recordings from the SC contralateral to the stimulated hemisphere revealed heterogeneous neuronal responses comprising short-latency excitation and delayed excitation or inhibition. Short-latency excitation was similar on trials with and without evoked movements, whereas delayed excitation was greater on trials that evoked eye or nose movements. Neurons modulated during spontaneous nose movements showed corresponding optogenetically evoked responses, linking stimulation-induced activity to endogenous movement-related activity. Thus, activation of SC GABAergic neurons initiates evolving population activity that recruits a coordinated sequence of orienting movements.
articles.author: Suyama, H., Lupashina, T., Hamon, M., Sibille, J., Teh, K. L., Liebert, K., Larkum, M. E., Sachdev, R., Kremkow, J.

articles.title: Imbalance between RNA-binding proteins and the WAVE regulatory complex underlies the toxic gain-of-function effects of the CYFIP2 Arg87Cys variant in neurodevelopmental disorders
articles.content: Pathogenic variants in cytoplasmic FMR1-interacting protein 2 (CYFIP2) cause neurodevelopmental disorders, with hotspot substitutions at arginine 87 (Arg87) associated with particularly severe symptoms. CYFIP2 functions both as a component of the WAVE (Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein family verprolin-homologous protein) regulatory complex (WRC), regulating the actin cytoskeleton, and as an interactor of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) involved in mRNA processing/translation. Although Arg87 variants reduce CYFIP2 protein stability, heterozygous knock-in mice carrying Arg87Cys (Cyfip2+/R87C) show markedly more severe phenotypes than heterozygous knockout (Cyfip2+/-) mice, supporting a toxic gain-of-function mechanism. However, how the dual roles of CYFIP2 contribute to this mechanism remains unclear. To address this, we examined Cyfip2+/R87C mice at postnatal week 7, before overt neuronal loss and gliosis, focusing on the progressive dispersion of hippocampal cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) pyramidal neurons, a phenotype absent in Cyfip2+/- mice. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing suggested candidate alterations related to translation and cell adhesion/migration in CA1 pyramidal neurons. Complementarily, human embryonic kidney 293T cells expressing CYFIP2 Arg87Cys showed defects in proliferation and morphology, accompanied by altered expression of cell adhesion-related genes. Quantitative proteomic analysis of the CA1 region uncovered an imbalance between CYFIP2-associated protein networks, characterized by increased RBPs and reduced WRC components. Phosphoproteomic analysis further revealed altered phosphorylation of synaptic and translational regulators. Consistently, whole-cell recordings and biocytin-based morphological analyses showed increased frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents and altered dendritic morphology in Cyfip2+/R87C CA1 pyramidal neurons, most prominently in the more severely dispersed deep-layer neurons. Moreover, the cell adhesion molecule Eph receptor A3 was reduced, possibly as a result of RBP dysregulation. Together, these findings suggest that an imbalance between RBP- and WRC-associated pathways underlies the gain-of-function effects of CYFIP2 Arg87Cys and contributes to early neuronal phenotypes, most notably CA1 layer dispersion. This mechanism, distinct from CYFIP2 haploinsufficiency, supports allele-specific therapeutic strategies for Arg87 variants.

articles.title: Impact of heat and sex on embryonic brain growth in dragons with temperature induced sex-reversal (Pogona vitticeps, Lacertilia: Agamidae)
articles.content: Climate warming can influence sex determination and embryonic growth in oviparous reptiles that rely on external temperatures during development. Warmer incubation temperatures can stimulate growth in ectotherms until oxygen supply can no longer keep pace with growth rate; at which point metabolically expensive organs like the brain suffer. We aimed to understand the impact of heat and sex on brain development in central bearded dragons, Pogona vitticeps (Agamidae), a uniquely thermosensitive species that exhibits sex-reversal at warm incubation temperatures. Three sexual phenotypes are possible in P. vitticeps: genetically driven ZW females and ZZ males, with the latter phenotype thermally overridden at incubation temperatures >32C to induce ZZ sex-reversed females. To visualise changes in brain anatomy, we used buffered Lugols iodine to perform contrast-enhanced micro computed tomography (microCT) and synchrotron propagation-based phase-contrast CT scanning. A total of 57 embryos were sampled across developmental stages and incubated at two temperature treatments: cool (28C, n = 26) and warm (36C, n = 21). Using high-resolution models of neuroanatomy, we found that the telencephalic region of the forebrain is significantly larger in individuals with ZZ genotypes (males and sex-reversed females) compared to concordant ZW females. Although incubation temperature significantly influenced growth rate and body size during development, overall brain size was not significantly different across temperature treatments. Our results indicate that the effects of genotypic sex on brain development are more important than thermal influences, and thus the brain may be somewhat buffered to the effects of warm incubation temperatures in this arid-adapted dragon.
articles.author: Hoops, D., Ceddia, A., Peters, R., Whiteley, S. L., Collin, S. P., Crowe-Riddell, J.

articles.title: Blue light compromises cellular fate of intrinsically photosensitive M&uumlller glial cells in the developing chicken retina.
articles.content: M&uumlller glial cells (MCs), the predominant glial population in the retina, interface with all neuronal types to form the structural and functional core of the tissue. Beyond their established homeostatic roles, MCs have emerged as promising endogenous neural stem cells with remarkable regenerative potential. Our recent work identified MCs as novel photosensitive elements of the vertebrate inner retina that express non-visual opsins and respond to brief light stimuli. Direct photic responses manifest as a sustained increase in intracellular calcium levels driven by a G protein-mediated signaling cascade that primarily recruits calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum, highlighting MC photoreception and its roles in retinal physiology. In the present work, we characterize expanded light-directed responses in primary chicken MC cultures, identifying a blue light (BL)-triggered signaling cascade. BL stimulation induces a peak in cAMP levels at 10 min, followed by CREB activation (p-CREB) within 30 min, a temporal profile consistent with observations in ex vivo retinal explants. BL exposure (1 h) at the onset of each cell cycle dampens proliferative capacity and migration while lengthening the cell cycle in both primary chicken MCs and an immortalized human MC cell line compared to dark controls. Furthermore, over time (24, 48, and 72 h), BL exposure reduces the proportion of pluripotent cells (Sox2 positive cells), concomitant with an increase in neuronal progenitors (Tbr2) and no change in glial markers (GS, RGR, GFAP). Finally, mature neuronal markers (TUJ-1 and Brn3) increase in MC cultures 120 h post-BL stimulation. Overall, this work broadens our understanding of BL-triggered signaling cascades in MCs and uncovers photoreception as a potential mechanism driving cell fate in the developing retina.
articles.author: Marchese, N. A., Rios, M. N., Yaneff, A., Davio, C., Guido, M. E.

articles.title: Spatially resolved single-cell atlas reveals cortical glial reactivity associated with regions of neuronal growth programs in both hemispheres after stroke
articles.content: Post-stroke recovery relies on structural remodeling of neuronal circuits in both the spared ipsilesional and contralesional cortices. RNA sequencing studies have identified distinct states of glial reactivity after stroke, but how these states are spatially organized at the single-cell level in relation to neuronal responses remains unknown. Consequently, it remains unclear which reactive states are lesion-restricted versus remote regions, such as the contralesional cortex, and how remote glial responses relate to the neuronal growth programs that support circuit repair. To address this, we used imaging-based subcellular spatial transcriptomics to profile ~650,000 cells across both hemispheres in male and female mice 7 days after cortical ischemic stroke, a critical timepoint for neuroplasticity. Reactive glial states differed significantly in their spatial organization from the lesion: scar-forming astrocytes and infiltrating pro-inflammatory myeloid cells were confined to the perilesional rim, whereas a reactive microglial state and a reactive astrocyte state extended into remote gray and white matter of the contralesional hemisphere. Mapping neuronal growth-associated gene expression across the entire cortex, we found substantial activation in both the perilesional and homotopic contralesional cortex, and these same regions showed significantly increased proportions of reactive microglia and astrocytes. Together, these findings identify spatially organized neuronal growth and glial activation states in both hemispheres after stroke and nominate regions for investigating spatial relationships between complex cell types and functional recovery.

articles.title: Goat Milk-derived Extracellular Vesicles modulate glial responses in vitro and attenuate neuroinflammation in vivo
articles.content: Milk-derived extracellular vesicles (MEV) represent a naturally derived, potentially scalable platform for immunomodulation, yet their effects on central nervous system (CNS) glial inflammation at defined particle-to-cell ratios remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated the immunomodulatory effects of goat milk-derived MEV in cellular and murine models of neuroinflammation. MEV-enriched preparations were obtained by sequential filtration, ultrafiltration, and size-exclusion chromatography, and characterized by scanning electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and dynamic light scattering. In LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia-like cells, MEV at 250 and 2500 particles per cell significantly reduced CD40 expression. In primary rat mixed glial cultures, microglia, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes internalized MEV. At 250 particles per cell, MEV significantly reduced CD40 and IL1{beta} gene expression at the mixed-culture level. In both cellular models, MEV also increased markers associated with an M2-like microglial phenotype under resting conditions. Following intrathecal administration in healthy mice, MEV did not induce significant changes in the inflammatory gene markers assessed at 8 h. In an LPS-induced mouse model of neuroinflammation, intrathecal MEV administration reduced CD40 protein expression towards control levels within 24 h and shifted the inflammatory marker profile towards a pro-resolutive state, as indicated by increased Arg1 levels and elevated CD206/CD86 and IL10/IL6 ratios. These findings identify goat milk-derived MEV-enriched preparations as potential modulators of CNS glial inflammation and support further investigation of their therapeutic potential.
articles.author: Santos-Coquillat, A., Lozano-Picazo, P., Iriarte-Urdiain, E., Yang, J., Ucakar, B., Mwema, A., Auquiere, M., des Rieux, A.

articles.title: Neuroinflammation is an early pathological process in a mouse model of prodromal Parkinsons disease
articles.content: Approximately 90% of Parkinson's disease (PD) patients exhibit olfactory deficits, which often precedes motor symptoms by years, and are a robust predictor for PD and subsequent cognitive decline. Pathological changes in the PD olfactory system, particularly synuclein (Syn) pathology in the olfactory bulb (OB) and severe involvement of the anterior olfactory nucleus (AON), are distinct from normal aging. However, the causal link between Syn aggregation and functional impairment, potentially involving cytotoxicity and neuroinflammation, remains elusive. To investigate these early pathological events, we utilized a prodromal PD model that we have previously characterized, involving the unilateral OB injection of Syn preformed fibrils (PFF) in wild-type mice. This triggers the transneuronal spread of pathogenic Syn, and olfactory dysfunction starting at 1-month post-injections. Here we report on neuropathological and inflammatory events 1-3 month following injection of PFFs into the OB. Following PFF injection, Syn pSer129 pathology progressively accumulated bilaterally in the AON and ipsilateral in the piriform cortex (PCX) over three months. Stereological quantification revealed no significant neuronal loss in the AON or PCX during this 1-3 month interval, indicating that olfactory impairment precedes overt neurodegeneration. Instead, we identified the upregulation of pro-inflammatory genes (Il-1{beta} ; and Il-6), significant microglial reactivity, and sustained astrogliosis within olfactory structures. These findings identify neuroinflammation as a key early mediator linking Syn pathology to olfactory dysfunction in the absence of neuronal loss. This suggests a critical window for therapeutic intervention and highlights neuroinflammatory markers as potential biomarkers for the prodromal phase of PD.
articles.author: Mercado, G., Stetzik, L., Schulz, E., Meyerdirk, L., Lindquist, A., Cohen, L., Escobar Galvis, M. L., Steiner, J. A., Moore, D. J., Wesson, D. J., Brundin, P.

articles.title: Pre-stress functional brain connectivity is associated with subsequent anxiety during war-related stress
articles.content: Individuals exposed to major real-world stressors show markedly different psychological outcomes, but whether this heterogeneity is associated with pre-existing neural characteristics remains unclear because neuroimaging is rarely performed beforehand. We acquired resting-state fMRI in healthy adults before the unforeseen onset of war-related stress. Approximately 13 months later, during ongoing war-related stress, participants (n = 31) were assessed for anxiety, depressive symptoms, perceived stress and post-traumatic stress symptoms. Among 144 associations spanning 36 predefined corticolimbic and reward-related connections and four outcomes, lower baseline functional connectivity between the right nucleus accumbens and right amygdala was associated with greater subsequent anxiety. This association survived permutation-based family-wise error correction and adjustment for baseline depressive symptoms, age and sex. These findings provide preliminary prospective evidence that pre-existing functional organization of threat- and reward-related circuitry is associated with individual differences in anxiety during prolonged adversity.
articles.author: Boshnak, N., Danan, N., Keren, H.

articles.title: Persistent cerebrovascular injury after preeclampsia in the STOX1A mouse model: implications for prokineticin signaling
articles.content: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-related hypertensive disorder associated with neurological complications that may persist beyond pregnancy. Prokineticins (PROK1 and PROK2) and their receptors (PROKR1 and PROKR2) regulate angiogenesis and inflammation and may be involved to PE-associated cerebrovascular injury. This study investigated alterations of the maternal brain prokineticin system during PE and 8 months postpartum, and assessed the consequences of prokineticin receptor inhibition using the PROKR antagonist PC1. Female WT FVB/N mice mated with transgenic males overexpressing STOX1A were used as a model of PE and received PC1 or vehicle during gestation. Circulating and regional brain PROK levels and receptor expression were assessed by ELISA and Western blotting. Long-term cerebral abnormalities were evaluated using high-resolution MRI and GFAP immunostaining. PE mice exhibited hypertension, proteinuria, reduced placental efficiency, and elevated circulating PROK1 and PROK2 levels. PC1 prevented hypertension and attenuated the elevation of circulating PROKs but did not prevent proteinuria or reduced placental efficiency. During PE, hippocampal PROK1 increased while PROK2 decreased; these changes persisted despite treatment. At 7 months postpartum, both PROKs were elevated in the cortex, and these increases were prevented by PC1. Region-specific changes in PROKR1 immunoreactivity and PROKR2 expression showed variable responses to treatment. MRI revealed hippocampal and parieto-temporal T2* hypointensities compatible with microhemorrhagic injury, post-contrast T1 abnormalities supporting blood-brain barrier disruption, and a distinct caudoputamen T1-hyperintense lesion potentially representing a nonhemorrhagic component. PC1 prevented focal cerebral lesions and associated astrocyte reactivity, whereas regional diffusion abnormalities persisted. These findings implicate prokineticin signaling in persistent PE-associated brain injury and support the potential of receptor antagonism to limit selected cerebral alterations.

Microglial NUS1 deficiency drives dopaminergic neurodegeneration through intercellular iron dysregulation in Parkinson’s disease models
articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02499-3

Using cellular and mouse models, this study reports that deficiency of the Parkinson’s disease risk gene NUS1 in microglia disrupts intercellular iron homeostasis, leading to neuronal iron overload and dopaminergic neurodegeneration.
articles.author: Haigang Ren

articles.title: Chronic progressive demyelination induces a microglial state with lysosomal dysfunction
articles.content:
Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 26 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02489-5

Acute myelin injury responses are well defined, but microglia adaptations to chronic damage remain unclear. Mouse models reveal a chronic demyelination-associated microglial state marked by inflammation, lysosomal dysfunction and myelin-damaging activity.
